FEATURE

By Luke Goodsell

Cartoonish Cruise ends up in a ham-fisted hole in Digger [https://www.thesaturdaypaper.com.au/culture/film/2026/09/30/cartoonish-cruise-ends-ham-fisted-hole-digger]

“How do you satirise something that’s already absurd?” If you had a dollar for the number of times you’d encountered a variation of this sentiment, whether in relation to the Trump administration or our Bond-villain technocrats, you’d likely be as rich as Digger Rockwell, the yeehaw oil baron at the centre of writer-director Alejandro González Iñárritu’s bombastic US$125 million satire.

A cartoonishly unrepentant tycoon in a stetson and cowboy boots, Digger is played, with no amount of subtlety, by American cinema’s fabled Last Movie Star, Tom Cruise.

As a satire – of rapacious capitalism, conservative politics, climate change denial, collect them all – the movie is an extended eye-roll, ham-fisted and relentlessly unfunny, which is also what Iñárritu appears to have set out to achieve.
